findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical parabola-aware two-pointer merge. It compares transformed endpoints, fills backward for convex or linear transforms and forward for concave transforms, and preserves duplicates with clear conventional state. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 360 and its Python sortTransformedArray surface. The Reference preserves sorted input, the exact quadratic transform, duplicate-preserving ascending output, both source examples, all three constraints, and the O(n) follow-up.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064599440. Its transform helper, output allocation, endpoint comparisons, branch directions, pointer and write updates, and return are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the required wrapper and annotations.

The legal convex-transform tiers use 16, 64, and 200 sorted values, span 12.5x, and force endpoint merging around the vertex. The current source passes all 14 executions at +0.01 relative growth and 1.05x; correct sorted-list insertion passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.71 and 5.65x.

The Approach accurately derives endpoint extrema from parabola shape, handles convex, concave, and linear coefficients, proves the output-boundary invariant, and states O(n) time with O(n) returned storage and O(1) auxiliary state.

The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples in order, the exact transform and sorted-output contract, all three constraints, and the source-native linear-time follow-up.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact inputs and outputs; the invented third sample is now correctly labelled a trial.
Visible boundaries cover nums.length=1, input values -100 and 100, and both -100 and 100 for each of a, b, and c; generated checks also cover nums.length=200.
Convex, concave, increasing-linear, decreasing-linear, and constant transforms exercise every shape branch, including vertices inside the input interval.
Duplicate inputs, equal transformed endpoints, an off-center vertex, and output ties verify that multiplicity and ascending order are preserved.

An independent direct transform-and-sort oracle verified all eleven authored results, all three benchmarks, 98,875 exhaustive small inputs, and 27 extreme-coefficient combinations at the 200-element maximum.
All eleven correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 16-, 64-, and 200-element workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
